metadata.title: JZ Mock D · Questions 1–2
metadata.description: A two-question preview with knowledge steps, pitfalls and similar exercises.

original.label: Paper 1 · Exercise 01
original.lead: Find the coefficient of <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></math> in the expansion of
original.formulaLabel: the quantity two minus x plus x squared over two, raised to the fifth power

hints.title: Choose a term from every bracket
hints.body: The expansion comes from choosing one term from each of the 5 brackets. A constant, linear or quadratic choice contributes power 0, 1 or 2 of x.
hints.recap: A term in the expansion is a product of one choice from each of the 5 brackets. Track the power of x from each choice: 0, 1 or 2.
hints.pitfall: Each bracket contributes exactly one choice to a product; do not take two terms from the same bracket.
hints.pause: Work out one possible selection on paper before continuing.

recall.reminder: Each product in an expansion takes one term from every bracket.

hints.title: List every way to reach the target power
hints.body: Let q brackets supply the quadratic term and l supply the linear term. Their total power is 2q + l. Set that equal to 4; the remaining brackets supply the constant.
hints.recap: List all nonnegative integer choices of quadratic and linear counts that reach the required power without using more than 5 brackets.
hints.pitfall: Finding one valid pattern does not prove it is the only one.
hints.pause: List the permitted counts before evaluating their contributions.

recall.reminder: Find all selections whose powers add to the required power; several selections may contribute to one coefficient.

hints.title: Count where each choice goes
hints.body: For each power pattern, choose its quadratic brackets first. Then choose its linear brackets from the remaining ones. Multiply these two selection counts; all remaining brackets supply the constant.
hints.recap: Use successive binomial choices to count the bracket positions for each distinct power pattern.
hints.pitfall: Repeated choices are indistinguishable: do not count swaps of identical terms as new arrangements.
hints.pause: Work out the arrangement count for each pattern.

recall.reminder: A binomial coefficient counts which brackets supply a chosen term. Choose the next type from the brackets still available.

hints.title: Include the numerical factors and add
hints.body: For each pattern, multiply its arrangement count by the numerical part of every selected term, including signs and fractions where present. Then add the contributions.
hints.recap: Multiply each arrangement count by its chosen coefficients and add all the contributions to obtain the required coefficient.
hints.pitfall: Keep the minus sign from every linear choice; an even number of them gives a positive product. Keep the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math> from every quadratic choice.
hints.pause: Finish the calculation on paper.

recall.reminder: Keep the selection count and every numerical factor, including signs and powers, before adding the contributions.

original.solution:
Worked calculation

These are all the ways for the selected powers to total 4:

Powers chosenCount and numerical valueContribution
1+1+1+1+05×2×(−1)410
2+1+1+0+030×(2)2×(−1)2×1260
2+2+0+0+010×(2)3×(12)220

For example, choose 1 of the 5 brackets for the quadratic term (5 ways), then 2 of the remaining 4 for the linear term (6 ways). That gives 30 arrangements for this pattern.

Total coefficient: 10 + 60 + 20 = 90.
original.source: Source: JZ Maths Mock Set D, Paper 1, Question 1.

original.label: Paper 1 · Exercise 02
original.lead: How many solutions are there to the equation
original.formulaLabel: absolute value of tangent x plus one over tangent x equals 3

hints.title: Use one variable and check the domain
hints.body: Let t=tanx. The equation only makes sense where tan x is defined and t is not zero.
hints.recap: Set <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>tan</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> so the equation becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math>. Keep <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> and exclude angles where tangent is undefined.
hints.pitfall: Keep the restriction that t is nonzero and that tangent is defined throughout the substitution.
hints.pause: Write the equation in terms of t on paper.

recall.reminder: Replace a repeated expression with one variable and carry its restrictions with it.

hints.title: Split the absolute value into two cases
hints.body: For t>0, solve t2−3t+1=0. For t<0, solve t2+3t−1=0. Keep only roots with the sign assumed.
hints.recap: Use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. This gives the two quadratics shown below. Check each root against its case.
hints.pitfall: Squaring or ignoring the sign condition can add roots that do not satisfy the original equation.
hints.pause: Write both quadratics on paper.

recall.reminder: Work in separate sign cases when a rule depends on whether a quantity is positive or negative.

hints.title: Keep only the roots allowed by each case
hints.body: Use the discriminant to decide whether each case equation has real roots. If it does, solve it and check every root against the sign assumed for that case.
hints.recap: The discriminant counts real candidates; the case restriction decides which candidates are allowed. Count distinct roots only.
hints.pitfall: A real root of a case equation is not automatically valid for that sign case.
hints.pause: Find and keep the permitted t-values from both cases.

recall.reminder: The discriminant gives the number of real roots. Then check which roots satisfy the conditions of the question.

hints.title: Count angles for each valid tangent value
hints.body: Tangent repeats every 180°. Sketch its branches over the stated interval and use the permitted t-values from your two cases as horizontal levels.
hints.recap: Count where each valid horizontal level meets the tangent graph on the allowed interval, handling endpoints and asymptotes separately.
hints.pitfall: A quadratic root is a tangent value, not yet an angle; 90° and 270° are undefined for tangent.
hints.pause: Count the angles for your admissible t-values, then combine the counts.

recall.reminder: Tangent repeats every 180 degrees. Count each admissible value across the whole stated interval.

original.solution:
Worked calculation

Put t=tanx. Tan x must be defined and t≠0.

CaseEquation and valid rootsAngles
t>0t2−3t+1=0. The roots are 3±52; both are positive.4
t<0t2+3t−1=0. The permitted root is t=−3−132. The other root is positive, so it does not belong to this case.2

Total: 4 + 2 = 6 solutions. Every permitted nonzero t-value gives two angles because tan repeats every 180°.
